root_cause.text: The amdxdna runtime PM reference was acquired inside the queued job execution path (`aie2_sched_job_run`), allowing a running workqueue job to call `pm_runtime_resume_and_get()` while the runtime suspend callback was simultaneously draining that same workqueue, causing a deadlock.
root_cause.evidence: The commit/CVE explicitly states “The runtime suspend callback drains the running job workqueue... If a job is still executing and calls pm_runtime_resume_and_get(), it can deadlock,” and the patch removes `amdxdna_pm_resume_get()`/`amdxdna_pm_suspend_put()` from `aie2_sched_job_run`/completion paths and moves the PM get to `amdxdna_cmd_submit()` before the job is queued.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove an incorrect PM suspend put from job completion notification to avoid prematurely dropping the device power-management reference.
intent_record.what: The call to amdxdna_pm_suspend_put(job->hwctx->client->xdna); was removed from aie2_sched_notify(), leaving the trace call, increment of job->hwctx->priv->completed, and dma_fence_signal(fence) unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this function no longer releases a power-management suspend reference when a scheduled job notification is processed, preventing the device's PM usage count from being decremented at this point and changing the power-management lifecycle associated with job completion.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove premature power-management resume/put handling from the scheduler job run path so early validation failures return immediately without unnecessary or mismatched PM reference management.
intent_record.what: The change removes the call to amdxdna_pm_resume_get(hwctx->client->xdna) and the associated error check, and also removes matching amdxdna_pm_suspend_put(hwctx->client->xdna) calls from the early-return paths when hwctx->priv->mbox_chann is missing or mmget_not_zero(job->mm) fails. The mailbox channel check is simplified to return NULL directly, and the mmget_not_zero failure path now returns ERR_PTR(-ESRCH) directly.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this function no longer acquires a power-management resume reference before validating prerequisites, and it no longer releases that reference on those early exits. This avoids performing PM resume/suspend reference management in this path and prevents failures or balancing requirements tied to amdxdna_pm_resume_get/put when the job cannot proceed due to a missing mailbox channel or dead mm.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove an erroneous PM suspend release from aie2_sched_job_run() error cleanup to prevent mismatched power-management reference handling.
intent_record.what: The change removes a single call to amdxdna_pm_suspend_put(hwctx->client->xdna) from the error-handling block guarded by if (ret) in aie2_sched_job_run().
intent_record.how: On the failure path of aie2_sched_job_run(), the function no longer decrements or releases the PM suspend reference for hwctx->client->xdna at that point, avoiding an extra suspend-put operation during error cleanup.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add the amdxdna power-management header to expose PM-related definitions needed by this source file.
intent_record.what: A single header include was added to the file: `#include "amdxdna_pm.h"` immediately after the existing `amdxdna_pci_drv.h` include.
intent_record.how: At runtime this has no direct behavioral effect by itself; functionally it makes declarations, macros, or types from the power-management header available to this compilation unit so code in the file can reference PM-related interfaces or satisfy build dependencies.

intent_record.intent_summary: Release the XDNA PM suspend hold during scheduler job cleanup to fix a missing power-management reference drop.
intent_record.what: A call to amdxdna_pm_suspend_put(job->hwctx->client->xdna) was added in amdxdna_sched_job_cleanup() immediately after the debug trace and before releasing job buffer objects, command buffer object, and fence references.
intent_record.how: This decrements or releases a previously held power-management suspend-prevention reference when a scheduled job is cleaned up, allowing the device to resume normal suspend behavior and preventing leaked PM usage holds after job completion or teardown.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a power-management resume check to command submission so it aborts cleanly if the device cannot be resumed.
intent_record.what: A call to amdxdna_pm_resume_get(xdna) was added before acquiring the SRCU read lock and loading the hardware context, along with an error check that logs "Resume failed, ret %d" and jumps to the put_bos cleanup path if the call fails.
intent_record.how: This change ensures the device power-management resume reference is obtained before continuing command submission, so submission does not proceed while the device is not successfully resumed; on resume failure, it aborts early, logs the error, and releases previously acquired resources through existing cleanup.

intent_record.intent_summary: Release the xdna PM suspend reference in the command submission cleanup path to fix a missing power-management put on failure.
intent_record.what: A call to amdxdna_pm_suspend_put(xdna) was added after srcu_read_unlock(&client->hwctx_srcu, idx), and a new label put_bos: was inserted immediately before the existing amdxdna_arg_bos_put(job) cleanup step.
intent_record.how: This updates the error or cleanup path so that a previously acquired power-management suspend reference on xdna is released before buffer objects are put, preventing an unmatched suspend hold and associated resource or power-state leak during command submission failure handling.

Add the amdxdna power-management header to expose PM-related definitions needed by this source file.

consistency_review.core_intent: Correct mismatched XDNA power-management suspend/resume reference handling across scheduler and command submission error/cleanup paths by removing erroneous puts and adding the missing cleanup release.

relevance_review.reason: The root cause is incorrect runtime PM reference handling in the scheduler job run path, specifically around acquiring/releasing PM refs during queued work execution. This group directly changes PM suspend/resume get/put behavior in aie2_sched_job_run and related scheduler cleanup/error paths, removing erroneous puts and relocating cleanup releases, which is directly tied to the flawed PM reference management that led to the deadlock.

This change only adds a power-management header include to expose PM definitions. It does not alter when or where the runtime PM reference is acquired, nor does it address the workqueue/runtime suspend deadlock root cause.

The change directly concerns runtime PM during command submission/job start, adding a resume check so execution does not proceed when the device cannot be resumed. Since the root cause is a deadlock around acquiring the runtime PM reference in the queued job execution path, this PM-resume handling is directly related to that vulnerability.

candidates.rationale: This is the core vulnerable statement: it acquires the runtime PM reference inside the queued scheduler job run path, which can execute concurrently with runtime suspend draining the same workqueue, creating the deadlock described in the root cause.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement acquires the runtime PM reference from within the queued scheduler job execution path. Per the root cause, doing so allowed the workqueue job to invoke runtime resume while the runtime suspend callback was concurrently draining that same workqueue, creating the deadlock.
